requirements.requirement: Build an IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the shared transit network
requirements.summary: swanctl -l on both node1 and node2 shows an IKEv2 SA in ESTABLISHED state over the transit addresses 10.10.10.1/10.10.10.2, and an ESP child SA in INSTALLED state (cmd-cc49bd69d1c74499, cmd-2a2782e6c1dd4546). Tunnel setup used the OPNsense REST API to create matching Connection/local/remote/child/PSK objects on both firewalls (cmd-03609eb1e245465b, cmd-2ccc996ddbf149ec, cmd-11bafc9bcd25473b, cmd-236429ad60064e3a, cmd-7f66c9377e1d4361, cmd-d65f6b1cda9f489b, cmd-523e865b095c4ec0, cmd-04d1888680ab4274, cmd-6a435aa5425b44b2).

requirements.requirement: Carry the private networks (lan-a 10.200.1.0/24, lan-b 10.200.2.0/24) over the tunnel
requirements.summary: The established child SA's local_ts/remote_ts fields show 10.200.1.0/24 <-> 10.200.2.0/24 on both node1 and node2 (cmd-cc49bd69d1c74499, cmd-2a2782e6c1dd4546), confirming the tunnel policy encapsulates the two private subnets rather than only the transit addresses.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 can reach each other by their private addresses
requirements.summary: Bidirectional ICMP connectivity was directly observed: node3 (10.200.1.12) to node4 (10.200.2.13) succeeded 5/5 (cmd-6a392f47680e4aae) and node4 to node3 succeeded (cmd-64aa1c33e5f147b7), both after the tunnel and routes were in place. A prior baseline attempt without the tunnel/rules established failed 100% (cmd-3c7811338c1b47dc), showing the private path only worked once the tunnel was functional.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the private networks is encrypted in transit across the shared transit network
requirements.summary: A tcpdump capture on the transit interface (vtnet1) during an active node3<->node4 ping showed only ESP packets between 10.10.10.1 and 10.10.10.2, with no plaintext ICMP visible (cmd-eee411791cb748bf), directly confirming the private traffic is encapsulated and encrypted on the shared link.

requirements.requirement: Private networks have no path between them except via the built tunnel (isolation preserved)
requirements.summary: A ping from node3 to node4's private address before the tunnel/rules were functional failed 100% (cmd-3c7811338c1b47dc), and later a similar ping before enc0 pass rules were added also failed (cmd-3bf68bfe36d24120), consistent with no pre-existing direct route between lan-a and lan-b outside the tunnel.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are directly satisfied by observed evidence: an IKEv2/ESP IPsec tunnel is established between node1 and node2 over the transit network, the tunnel's traffic selectors carry the lan-a and lan-b private subnets, node3 and node4 achieve bidirectional ICMP reachability by private address, and a tcpdump capture on the transit link during live traffic shows only ESP packets (no plaintext), confirming encryption in transit. Isolation before the tunnel was functional was also directly observed as failing, consistent with the stated topology constraint. Independently, the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol was executed and captured in full for all four nodes: each shows a pre-restart boot identity/health baseline, an explicit restart action, an SSH/connection failure during the reboot window, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered interface/firewall/IPsec/tunnel-connectivity state. These restart observations are corroborated by the independent fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot's boot-identity values, which match the executor's own before/after markers for all four nodes.
limitations: The public task contract does not require reboot persistence, so the restart-protocol evidence (while complete and well-corroborated) is treated as supplemental quality information rather than a scored task requirement.

Two firewall pass rules involving 'ipsec'/'enc0' interface naming and blockpriv/blockbogons required several iterative corrective edits before converging on a working configuration; the final state is confirmed working, but the intermediate attempts show some trial-and-error rather than a single deliberate design.

Root-scoped OPNsense API keys generated to drive configuration remain persisted in config.xml on node1/node2 after task completion; this is a reasonable implementation choice but was not reviewed or revoked as a security follow-up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were almost entirely purposeful and causally tied to building the tunnel: interface/IP assignment on node1/node2 (cmd-e46d4421338640f1, cmd-840c8c5e7428480e), disabling blockpriv/blockbogons that were blocking the RFC1918 transit/private addresses (cmd-911027aeb0b84554, cmd-7a41c0cc45cc4278), iterative firewall-rule fixes to actually pass IKE/ESP/decrypted traffic (cmd-c1629ba1f6da41a8, cmd-105a04ebb0fe4c7f through cmd-9d61f3bbe4f64ee0), and persisted static routes on node3/node4 via systemd-networkd (cmd-327cb4a04f54413b, cmd-ceb550497d5446e1). Diagnostic tcpdump captures were cleaned up (cmd-dddf49a017804127, cmd-5a95a6a0210d4a8d, cmd-eec7227d0d2d4562, cmd-6a1cd867921d48b6) and temporary python helper scripts were removed. Two residual items remain and were not reverted: (1) config.xml.bak-* backup files created via shutil.copy before each XML edit (cmd-69f60e1b00a647ce, cmd-156b6602a21048c9, cmd-c1629ba1f6da41a8) were left on disk on node1/node2 -- low-risk, standard precautionary backups, not cleaned up; (2) a new root-scoped OPNsense API key/secret was generated and persisted in config.xml on both firewalls (cmd-69f60e1b00a647ce, cmd-ee0a5568bc4440b1) to drive IPsec configuration -- a plausible, necessary implementation choice to reach the swanctl API but leaves a standing privileged credential that was not revoked after use. Neither issue caused conflicting services, broken package state, or unsafe exposure of the tunnel itself.
